justification: redundant guard: noDuplicateMembers has already walked the whole document with Decoder.Token, which enforces the same syntax and the same 10000-level depth limit (observed: 10001 levels still rejected, text "exceeded max depth", with this guard disabled); no input reaches Decode that Token accepted and Decode rejects (probed on go1.26.8; other toolchains UNCONFIRMED)
after Decoder.Token inside an object the next token is a string key or an error; an error is returned by the preceding guard (C09 kills that one), so a non-string key token cannot reach here

decoder errors are sticky (Decoder.err): a failing Decode makes the next Token (the closing-token guard, killed by C13) return the same error text; observed identical message for {"signature":1,"a":} with this guard disabled
same argument as withoutTopLevelMember: a key token inside an object is a string or an error already returned by the guard before it (C21 kills that one)
the switch is entered only for a json.Delim returned at a value position; Token reports only { or [ there, a closing delimiter at a value position is a syntax error returned before
values come from Decode into any with UseNumber: nil, bool, json.Number, string, []any, map[string]any only; every other type is impossible
when all digits are zero this early return gives "0"; with it disabled TrimLeft empties digits and the second guard returns the same "0" (sign dropped in both); outputs identical
digits is non-empty after the first guard and its last character is a non-zero digit (trailing zeros were trimmed), so TrimLeft of zeros cannot empty it
raw is a complete JSON string value already validated by the enclosing decode; unmarshalling it into a string cannot fail
second decode of an already-decoded object into map[string]json.RawMessage cannot fail

the same bytes were already decoded into the typed License.Encryption struct (text_hint string); the *string field accepts every input the string field does, so the second decode cannot fail where the first succeeded (observed survivor X18)
bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword fails only for input over 72 bytes and Register rejects longer passwords first
